summary: The preprint develops fixed-degree counting of integer polynomials by Galois group using permutation indices, powerful discriminants, finite-field Fourier estimates and a three-case sieve. The corrected principal scope is n≥3, transitive groups for number-field exponents, and the explicit application restrictions below. This independent review changes the extraction to partial: 74 items, 10 library, 3 planned and 61 missing, each missing item routed once across six routes. Five source routes have usable ownership contracts. The Part II is rejected pending its elimination proof, recursive suppliers, declaration splitting and definition APIs/tests. All 26 findings are checked against arXiv v3 only; E11 and E13 are proof failures, not disproved counting theorems. The published article was not obtained.

items.name: The counts E_n(H) and N_n(G, H)
items.statement: For fixed n ≥ 2 and H ≥ 1, E_n(H) counts monic integer polynomials of degree n with nonleading coefficients bounded by H whose Galois group is not S_n. For a subgroup G ≤ S_n, N_n(G,H) counts separable such polynomials whose root action is conjugate to G. Repeated-root polynomials are included in E_n(H); their treatment separately from the n-letter action is required. The lower bound E_n(H) ≫ H^{n−1} follows by taking a_n = 0 and a separable complementary factor. The O(H^{n−1}) theorem is restricted to n ≥ 3 (E26). For irreducible f, put K_f=Q[x]/(f), D=|Disc(K_f)| and C=rad(D); item 22 identifies the primes in C with ramification.
items.sourceStatement: For H ≥ 1, E_n(H) is the number of monic f(x) = x^n + a_1x^{n−1} + ··· + a_n ∈ Z[x] with max|a_i| ≤ H whose Galois group G_f is not S_n, and for a permutation group G ⊂ S_n, N_n(G, H) is the number of such f with G_f ≅ G as permutation groups. Trivially E_n(H) ≫ H^{n−1} (take a_n = 0).

items.name: Galois group of a polynomial as a permutation group of its roots
items.statement: For f ∈ Q[x] of degree n with distinct roots, G_f = Gal(f) acts faithfully on the n roots in a splitting field, which makes G_f a permutation group on n letters well defined up to conjugacy in S_n.

items.name: Primitive permutation groups; primitivity versus subfields
items.statement: A transitive group on n > 1 letters is primitive if its invariant partitions are trivial. For a separable polynomial f of positive degree, the Galois action on its roots is transitive iff f is irreducible. For irreducible f of degree > 1, that action is primitive iff Q(α) has no intermediate field strictly between Q and Q(α).
items.note: Tau Ceti proves the Galois action on the roots of an irreducible separable p of degree > 1 is preprimitive iff F(α) is an atom (no intermediate field).
items.sourceStatement: A transitive G ⊂ S_n is primitive if it preserves no nontrivial partition of {1, …, n}. For irreducible f, G_f is intransitive exactly when f factors over Q (so an irreducible f has transitive G_f), and a transitive G_f is imprimitive exactly when Q[x]/(f(x)) has a proper subfield other than Q.

items.name: Index of a permutation and of a permutation group
items.statement: For g ∈ S_n, ind(g) := n − (number of orbits of g on {1, …, n}); for a nontrivial permutation group G, ind(G) := min_{1 ≠ g ∈ G} ind(g). Equivalently ind(g) = n minus the number of cycles of g including fixed points; ind(G) = 1 iff G contains a transposition.
items.sourceStatement: For g ∈ S_n, ind(g) := n − (number of orbits of g on {1, …, n}); for a permutation group G, ind(G) := min_{1 ≠ g ∈ G} ind(g). Equivalently ind(g) = n minus the number of cycles of g including fixed points; ind(G) = 1 iff G contains a transposition.

items.name: k-powerful integers
items.statement: For k ≥ 1, a positive integer N is k-powerful if every prime dividing N occurs to exponent at least k. Squarefull and cubefull mean k = 2 and 3. Counting and convergent-tail estimates in item 52 require k ≥ 2.
items.sourceStatement: An integer N is k-powerful if p^k | N for every prime p | N; 2-powerful integers are called squarefull and 3-powerful cubefull.

items.name: Number-field counts F_n(G, X), admissible exponents a(G), and Malle's conjecture
items.statement: For n ≥ 2 and a transitive G ≤ S_n, F_n(G,X) counts Q-isomorphism classes of degree-n number fields with root action G and absolute discriminant at most X. An admissible exponent a(G) > 0 satisfies F_n(G,X) = O_G(X^{a(G)}). Malle's weak conjecture predicts X^{1/ind(G)} ≪ F_n(G,X) ≪_ε X^{1/ind(G)+ε}; this is a conjectural target, not an unconditional counting theorem.
items.sourceStatement: F_n(G, X) is the number of number fields of degree n with associated Galois group G (as a permutation group) and absolute discriminant at most X; a(G) > 0 denotes any constant with F_n(G, X) = O(X^{a(G)}). Malle conjectured that one may take a(G) = 1/ind(G) + ε, and indeed X^{1/ind(G)} ≪ F_n(G, X) ≪ X^{1/ind(G)+ε}.

items.name: Elemental and non-elemental primitive permutation groups of type (r, m, k)
items.statement: A primitive G acting on Ω is non-elemental if there are positive integers r, m, k with k ≤ m/2 and (r > 1 or k > 1) such that Ω = ∆^r with ∆ the k-element subsets of {1, …, m}, n = C(m, k)^r, and G ⊂ S_m ≀ S_r acts by the natural automorphisms of this structure; otherwise G is elemental. G′ denotes the natural imprimitive action of the same group on rm letters; non-basic primitive groups (r > 1) are non-elemental.

items.name: Splitting types and their index, length and automorphism count
items.statement: A splitting type is a formal expression σ = (f_1^{e_1} ··· f_r^{e_r}); deg σ = Σ e_if_i, ind σ = Σ (e_i − 1)f_i, len σ = Σ f_i = deg σ − ind σ, and #Aut(σ) = ∏ f_i times the number of permutations of the factors f_i^{e_i} preserving σ (e.g. #Aut(1^1 2^5 2^5 2^5 3^1 1^1) = 288). The splitting type (f, p) of a binary form or polynomial f modulo p records its factorisation f ≡ ∏ P_i^{e_i}, deg P_i = f_i, and ind(f) modulo p is ind of (f, p).
items.sourceStatement: A splitting type is a formal expression σ = (f_1^{e_1} ··· f_r^{e_r}); deg σ = Σ e_if_i, ind σ = Σ (e_i − 1)f_i, len σ = Σ f_i = deg σ − ind σ, and #Aut(σ) = ∏ f_i times the number of permutations of the factors f_i^{e_i} preserving σ (e.g. #Aut(1^1 2^5 2^5 3^1 1^1) = 288). The splitting type (f, p) of a binary form or polynomial f modulo p records its factorisation f ≡ ∏ P_i^{e_i}, deg P_i = f_i, and ind(f) modulo p is ind of (f, p).
items.note: The preprint example has three factors 2^5. The earlier extraction omitted one: its displayed type has automorphism count 48, whereas the source type has 288.

items.name: Spaces of binary n-ic forms and monic polynomials, and their finite Fourier transforms
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, V_R is the rank n+1 coefficient module of binary n-ic forms, and V_R^1 is the affine space of monic degree-n polynomials. With d = n+1 or n respectively, q ≥ 2 and the standard coefficient pairing, Ψ̂_q(g) = q^{−d}Σ_f Ψ_q(f) exp(2πi⟨f,g⟩/q) on (Z/qZ)^d; M(Ψ_q) = max_{g≠0}|Ψ̂_q(g)|. Its periodic extension to integer frequencies distinguishes zero residue classes from the single frequency zero.
items.sourceStatement: V_R is the rank n + 1 module of binary n-ic forms over R and V^1_R ⊂ V_R the monic ones (identified with monic polynomials of degree n). For Ψ_q : V_{Z/qZ} → C, Ψ̂_q(g) = q^{−(n+1)} Σ_f Ψ_q(f) exp(2πi[f, g]/q) on the dual V*_{Z/qZ} (and with q^{−n} on V^1), and M(Ψ_q) = max_{g ≠ 0} |Ψ̂_q(g)|.

items.name: The weight functions w_{p,σ}
items.statement: For a splitting type σ = (f_1^{e_1} ··· f_r^{e_r}), w_{p,σ}(f) counts r-tuples (P_1, …, P_r) of distinct irreducible binary forms over F_p (each y or monic in x; in §4.2 monic polynomials), deg P_i = f_i, up to the permutations preserving σ, with P_1^{e_1} ··· P_r^{e_r} | f.

items.name: Height and Mahler measure of a monic polynomial
items.statement: For a monic complex polynomial f = x^n+a_1x^{n−1}+…+a_n, use H₊(f) = max(1,|a_1|,…,|a_n|), the sup norm of all coefficients, and M(f)=∏_r max(1,|r|), roots counted with multiplicity. Then binom(n,floor(n/2))^{−1}H₊(f) ≤ M(f) ≤ sqrt(n+1)H₊(f), M(fg)=M(f)M(g), and H₊(fg) is comparable to H₊(f)H₊(g) with constants depending only on the degrees. For H ≥ 1, this gives the same coefficient box as the original height.
items.sourceStatement: H(f) = max_i |a_i| and M(f) = ∏_k max{1, |r_k|} over the complex roots. Then C(n, ⌊n/2⌋)^{−1} H(f) ≤ M(f) ≤ √(n + 1) H(f), M is multiplicative, and hence H(fg) = Θ(H(f)H(g)) with constants depending on the degrees.
items.note: E20 corrects the source's zero-height exception. Mathlib's supNorm includes the leading coefficient.

items.name: Discriminants and resultants of polynomials
items.statement: Polynomial.discr and Polynomial.resultant provide the polynomial discriminant and resultant. For f of positive degree d, Res(f,f′)=(-1)^{d(d−1)/2}lc(f)Disc(f). The specialization to Disc_x(x^n+a_1x^{n−1}+…+a_n), including its degree n−1 and leading coefficient ±n^n in a_n, is a separate missing adapter in item 56.
items.sourceStatement: Disc(f) of a polynomial and the resultant Res; Disc_{a_n}(Disc_x(f(x))) = Res_{a_n}(Disc(f), ∂Disc(f)/∂a_n) up to the leading coefficient ±n^n of Disc(f) in a_n, which has degree n − 1 in a_n.

items.name: Number-field discriminant and integral primitive-element index formula
items.statement: For a number field K with an integral primitive element α and monic minimal polynomial f, Disc(f)=[O_K:Z[α]]² Disc(K). In the counting applications D=|Disc(K)|; the equality between ramification support and the prime support of D is imported separately via item 22.
items.note: The index-squared identity has an exact pinned Tau Ceti theorem for an integral primitive element. Identification of the ramified-prime product with the discriminant radical is imported from the number-field ramification interface; it is not supplied by NumberField.discr alone.
items.sourceStatement: For irreducible monic f, K_f = Q[x]/(f(x)), D = |Disc(K_f)|, and C is the product of the primes ramified in K_f (the radical of D); Disc(f) = [O_K : Z[x]/(f)]²·Disc(K_f).

items.name: The partition count q(k, n − k)
items.statement: For 0 ≤ k < n, q(k,n−k) counts partitions of k into at most n−k positive parts, equivalently partitions of n into exactly n−k positive parts (pad with zeros and add one to each part). It counts geometric root-multiplicity patterns, not all finite-field splitting types of index k. This filtered finite count and its bijection are missing adapters over Nat.Partition.
items.note: Nat.Partition is the carrier only. For n=4,k=1 the types (1^2 1^1 1^1) and (1^2 2^1) both occur, while q(1,3)=1; the former assertion about all splitting types was false.
items.sourceStatement: q(k, n − k) is the number of partitions of k into at most n − k parts, equivalently of partitions of n into exactly n − k parts; it is the constant c of Theorem 2 and bounds the number of splitting types of index k.

items.name: Hilbert irreducibility by height: E_n(H) = o(H^n)
items.statement: 100% of monic integer polynomials of degree n with coefficients in [−H, H] are irreducible with Galois group S_n: E_n(H) = o(H^n).

items.name: Reducible polynomials (van der Waerden): intransitive Galois groups
items.statement: For fixed n ≥ 3 the number of reducible monic integer polynomials of degree n in the coefficient box is O_n(H^{n−1}); separable reducible polynomials have intransitive root action. For n=2 the count is instead of order H log H. The finer Chela asymptotic and its exact degree-dependent remainder require collation of the cited source before use.
items.sourceStatement: Σ_{G ⊂ S_n intransitive} N_n(G, H) = O(H^{n−1}); the polynomials with intransitive Galois group are exactly the reducible ones (van der Waerden [43]; Chela [10] gives the asymptotic c_nH^{n−1} + O(H^{n−2})).
items.note: E26 restores the degree range. The earlier unqualified Chela remainder O(H^{n−2}) is not independently certified here.

items.name: Imprimitive Galois groups (Widmer)
items.statement: For fixed degree n, the number of monic integer polynomials of height at most H whose Galois action is transitive imprimitive is O_n(H^{n/2+2}), via number fields with a proper intermediate field (Widmer [46]). The even-polynomial example in the source supplies only a lower family of size H^{n/2}, not the matching exponent n/2+2.
items.sourceStatement: Σ_{G ⊂ S_n transitive, imprimitive} N_n(G, H) = O(H^{n/2+2}), essentially optimal (x^n + a_2x^{n−2} + ··· + a_n for even n); via number fields with a nontrivial subfield (Widmer [46]).
items.note: Do not claim a matching lower bound from the displayed family.

items.name: Proposition 9 (Jordan): primitive groups containing a transposition
items.statement: If G ⊂ S_n is primitive and contains a transposition, then G = S_n.

items.name: Proposition 10 (Jordan), 3-cycle case
items.statement: A primitive G ⊂ S_n containing a 3-cycle contains A_n, so G = A_n or S_n.

items.name: Proposition 10 (Jordan), double-transposition case
items.statement: If n ≥ 9 and a primitive G ⊂ S_n contains a double transposition, then G = A_n or S_n (Dixon–Mortimer [16, Theorem 3.3A and Example 3.3.1]).

items.name: Small indices of primitive groups
items.statement: If G ⊂ S_n is primitive and G ≠ S_n then ind(G) ≥ 2; if moreover G ≠ A_n and n ≥ 9 then ind(G) ≥ 3.

items.name: Inertia cycle type and discriminant valuation
items.statement: If p = ∏ P_i^{e_i} in K_f with residue degrees f_i and p is tamely ramified, a generator of an inertia group I_p ⊂ G_f ⊂ S_n has f_i cycles of length e_i and v_p(Disc K_f) = Σ (e_i − 1)f_i; if p is wildly ramified then v_p(Disc K_f) > Σ (e_i − 1)f_i ≥ ind(g) for all g ∈ I_p. When p does not divide the index [O_K : Z[α]], f mod p factors as p does (Dedekind–Kummer).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 11, p. 8; §5 Case III, p. 24 (arXiv v3)

items.name: Proposition 11: the index of the Galois group makes the discriminant powerful
items.statement: If ind(Gal(f)) = k then Disc(K_f) is k-powerful. Hence, if an irreducible f of degree n has primitive Galois group G ≠ S_n then Disc(K_f) is squarefull, and if G ≠ A_n, S_n and n ≥ 9 it is cubefull.
items.locator: Proposition 11 and the paragraph after it, p. 8 (arXiv v3)

items.name: Minimal degree of primitive groups (Liebeck–Saxl)
items.statement: A non-identity element of a primitive G ⊂ S_n with G ≠ A_n, S_n moves more than 2(√n − 1) points ([29, Cor. 3]; CFSG).

items.name: Theorem 12: ind(G) ≥ ⌊√n⌋
items.statement: If G ⊂ S_n is primitive and G ≠ A_n, S_n then ind(G) ≥ ⌊√n⌋. The bound is attained for all square n = m² ≥ 25 by S_m ≀ S_2 acting on the m² entries of an m × m matrix (ind = m).

items.name: Minimal degree of elemental primitive groups (Guralnick–Magaard)
items.statement: A non-identity element of an elemental primitive G ⊂ S_n with G ≠ A_n, S_n moves at least 3n/7 points, with equality for O_7(2) on n = 28 points; at least 4n/9 if n ≠ 28 (equality O_8^−(2), n = 27), at least 7n/15 if n > 28 (equality O_8^+(2), n = 120), and at least n/2 if n < 27 ([21], building on [29, Theorem 2]; CFSG).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 13 and Remark 14, p. 9 (arXiv v3)

items.name: Theorem 13 and Remark 14: indices of elemental primitive groups
items.statement: If G ⊂ S_n is elemental primitive, G ≠ A_n, S_n, then ind(G) ≥ 3n/14, sharp for O_7(2), n = 28 (a transvection is a product of 6 transpositions); moreover ind(G) ≥ 2n/9 if n ≠ 28, ind(G) ≥ 7n/30 if n > 28, and ind(G) ≥ n/4 if n < 27.

items.name: Babai's minimal-degree bound and the CFSG-free thresholds
items.statement: Without CFSG: a non-identity element of a primitive G ⊂ S_n, G ≠ A_n, S_n, moves at least (√n − 1)/2 points ([3, 6.14]), so ind(G) ≥ (√n − 1)/4. Theorems 12–13 for n ≤ 35 follow without CFSG from the Jordan–Manning classification of primitive groups having an element of support ≤ 14 ([32]–[37]; [47] for prime support). Only the threshold 53 of Corollary 3(a) (replaceable by 1090) and Corollary 3(c) (replaceable by O(H^{n−b√n})) use CFSG.

items.name: Theorem 16: indices in a non-elemental group versus its imprimitive companion
items.statement: Let G ⊂ S_m ≀ S_r be non-elemental primitive of type (r, m, k) on n = C(m, k)^r letters (1 ≤ k < m/2) and G′ its imprimitive action on rm letters. For every non-identity g ∈ G with image g′ ∈ G′, ind(g)/ind(g′) > n/(3rm). The proof uses f(m, k, y) ≥ (8/(5k))·C(m − 1, k − 1)·y (6) for the number f(m, k, y) of k-subsets of {1, …, m} moved by a product of y disjoint transpositions (see E5 for the induction).

items.name: Corollary 17: ind(g)/ind(g′) ≫ √n
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 16, ind(g)/ind(g′) ≥ n/(3rm) ≫ n^{1/2}, with exponent 1/2 optimal (attained for {r, k} = {1, 2}).

items.name: Corollary 18: discriminants of non-elemental fields and their resolvents
items.statement: If K has degree n = C(m, k)^r and Galois group a non-elemental primitive G of type (r, m, k), and K′ ⊂ L (the Galois closure) is the G′-resolvent of degree rm, then |Disc K| ≫_n |Disc K′|^{n/(3rm)} ≫ |Disc K′|^{c√n}.

items.name: Schmidt's bound for number fields of degree n
items.statement: F_n(G, X) = O(X^{(n+2)/4}) for every n > 1 and every G (Schmidt [39]).

items.name: Lemke Oliver–Thorne bound for number fields of degree n
items.statement: There is r > 0 with F_n(G, X) = O(X^{r log² n}) for all n and G, which beats Schmidt's bound for n ≥ 95 (Lemke Oliver–Thorne [28]).

items.name: Schmidt's small trace-zero element
items.statement: For n ≥ 2 a degree-n number field K of absolute discriminant D has a nonzero nonrational integral trace-zero element α with archimedean L² norm ≪_n D^{1/(2n−2)}. If K has no proper intermediate field, α generates K, and its degree-n minimal polynomial has a_1=0 and |a_i| ≪_n D^{i/(2n−2)}. The generator conclusion needs this additional hypothesis.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 20, p. 15 (as in [39]) (arXiv v3)
items.sourceStatement: A number field K of degree n and absolute discriminant D contains α ∈ O_K − Z of trace zero with ‖α‖ ≪ D^{1/(2n−2)}, where ‖·‖ is the L² norm over the archimedean embeddings; its minimal polynomial x^n + a_2x^{n−2} + ··· + a_n then has |a_i| ≪ D^{i/(2n−2)}.
items.note: The proof of Theorem 20 assumes primitivity. The extraction had incorrectly extended the generator conclusion to every number field.

items.name: Proposition 22: weighted power sums
items.statement: If m_1, …, m_r ∈ L are such that no nonempty subset sums to 0, then for all c_1, …, c_r ∈ L the system Σ_i m_i x_i^j = c_j (j = 1, …, r) (7) has at most r! solutions in L̄ (only x = 0 when all c_j = 0).

items.name: Bézout bound for zero-dimensional complete intersections in projective space
items.statement: If r homogeneous polynomials of degrees d_1, …, d_r on P^r over an algebraically closed field cut out a zero-dimensional scheme, it has at most d_1 ··· d_r points.

items.name: Girard–Newton identities
items.statement: The first r elementary symmetric functions of n quantities determine, and are determined by, their first r power sums over a ring in which r! is invertible.

items.name: Remark 23: the index strata of monic polynomials
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero or greater than n, and 0 ≤ k < n, the closed locus of monic degree-n polynomials with geometric index at least k has components given by multiplicity partitions of n into n−k parts: the images of (r_i) ↦ ∏(x−r_i)^{m_i}, each of dimension n−k. Each spans the coefficient affine space. Use the monic normalization t^{−n}f(tx+c) for t ≠ 0. For binary forms the corresponding projective locus is the image of (P¹)^{n−k} in P(V); the affine locus includes the scalar cone.
items.sourceStatement: Over an algebraically closed L with char L ∤ n!, the irreducible components of the variety of monic polynomials of degree n having index ≥ k are indexed by the partitions (m_1 ≥ ··· ≥ m_{n−k}) of n, each the image of A^{n−k} under (r_i) ↦ ∏ (x − r_i)^{m_i}, of dimension n − k; none lies in a hyperplane (through translates f(t(x + c)), a rational normal curve), and the same holds for binary n-ic forms with P^1 in place of A^1.
items.note: E22 fixes the normalization and the projective/affine distinction. Finite projections and specialization needed by §6 are a separate recorded gap.

items.name: Proposition 21: polynomials of given index are determined by their top coefficients
items.statement: Let P(x) = x^n + a_1x^{n−1} + ··· + a_n over a field K with char K ∤ n!. If a_1, …, a_{n−k} are fixed, at most q(k, n − k)·(n − k)! values of (a_{n−k+1}, …, a_n) ∈ K^k give P of index k over K (P = ∏ P_i^{e_i}, Σ (e_i − 1) deg P_i = k).

items.name: Lemma 24: discriminant valuation bounds the index modulo p
items.statement: Let g ∈ Z[x] be monic, separable and of degree n ≥ 1. Let D be the absolute discriminant of the maximal order in the finite étale Q-algebra Q[x]/(g). For every prime p > n, ind(g mod p) ≥ v_p(D). The integral and monic hypothesis is essential; see E18. In number-field applications g is irreducible.
items.sourceStatement: If g ∈ Z[x] and Q[x]/(g) has nonzero discriminant D, then for every prime p > n the index of g over F_p is at least v_p(D).
items.note: The tame proof uses v_p(D_i)=(e_i−1)f_i and geometric index e_i−1 for a monic local factor reducing to (x−c)^e, as corrected in E19.

items.name: Theorem 20: improved Schmidt bound for primitive groups
items.statement: If G is a primitive permutation group on n letters then F_n(G, X) = O_ε(X^{(n+2)/4 − 1 + 1/ind(G) + ε}). In particular one may take a(G) = (n + 2)/4 − 1 + 1/ind(G) + ε.

items.name: Theorem 25: counting non-elemental primitive fields
items.statement: If G ⊂ S_m ≀ S_r is non-elemental primitive of type (r, m, k) on n = C(m, k)^r letters, then F_n(G, X) = O(X^{b rm log²(rm)/n}) = O(X^{b log² n/√n}) for an absolute b > 0; also F_n(G, X) ≪_n F_rm(G′, X^{3rm/n}) = O(X^4) (8) by Schmidt's bound.

items.name: Twisted Poisson summation on boxes of forms and polynomials
items.statement: For d ≥ 1, q ≥ 2, H ≥ 1, Ψ on (Z/qZ)^d and Schwartz φ on R^d, with Fourier signs as in item 9, Σ_{f∈Z^d}Ψ(f)φ(f/H)=H^dΣ_{g∈Z^d}Ψ̂(g mod q)φ̂(gH/q). Splitting the right side into g∈qZ^d and g∉qZ^d gives |Σ_f Ψ(f)φ(f/H)| ≪_{φ,d} H^d|Ψ̂(0)|+q^d M(Ψ). The error after removing only g=0 cannot in general be bounded solely by M(Ψ).
items.note: E23 records zero-residue aliases. Import the archimedean Schwartz/Fourier interface from AL.0, extending pinned one-dimensional SchwartzMap.tsum_eq_tsum_fourier by iteration with absolute convergence.
items.sourceStatement: For Ψ_q on V_{Z/qZ} and a Schwartz function φ on R^{n+1}, Σ_{f ∈ V_Z} Ψ_q(f)φ(f/H) = H^{n+1} Σ_{g ∈ V*_Z} Ψ̂_q(g) φ̂(gH/q) (10), and the monic analogue (19) on Z^n; with φ̂(g) ≪_N ‖g‖^{−N} ([41, Ch. 5, Thm 1.3]) the error beyond the main term is O(q^{n+1+ε}M(Ψ_q)) (resp. O(q^{n+ε}M(Ψ_q))).
proofSteps: Obtain the lattice formula by successive one-dimensional Poisson summation; justify each interchange using Schwartz decay.
Finite Fourier inversion and orthogonality give the q-periodic twist with normalization q^{−d}.
Frequencies qh contribute H^d Ψ̂(0) Σ_h φ̂(Hh), bounded uniformly after factoring H^d since H≥1.
For all remaining frequencies use M(Ψ) and H^d Σ_{g≠0}(1+H||g||/q)^{−N} ≪_{N,d} q^d for N>d.

items.name: Proposition 26: Fourier transform of w_{p,σ} on binary forms
items.statement: For a splitting type σ with 1 ≤ deg σ = d ≤ n, ind σ = k, len σ = ℓ and p > n: ŵ_{p,σ}(0) = p^{−k}/#Aut(σ) + O(p^{−(k+1)}) and ŵ_{p,σ}(g) = O(p^{−(k+1)}) for g ≠ 0.
items.sourceStatement: For a splitting type σ with deg σ = d, ind σ = k, len σ = ℓ and p > n: ŵ_{p,σ}(0) = p^{−k}/#Aut(σ) + O(p^{−(k+1)}) and ŵ_{p,σ}(g) = O(p^{−(k+1)}) for g ≠ 0.

items.name: Corollaries 27–29: equidistribution of binary forms of large index modulo primes
items.statement: The number of integral binary n-ic forms in [−H, H]^{n+1} of index ≥ k modulo p is O_ε(H^{n+1}/p^k + p^{n−k+ε}) (27); for D = ∏ p_i^{k_i} and C = ∏ p_i, those of index ≥ k_i modulo every p_i number O_ε(c^{ω(C)}H^{n+1}/D + C^ε ∏ p_i^{n−k_i}) (28), which is O(c^{ω(C)}H^{n+1}/D) if C < H^{1+δ} with 0 < δ < 1/n (29). Here H ≥ 1, primes p_i are distinct and > n, and 1 ≤ k_i < n; empty or impossible index strata are treated separately.
items.sourceStatement: The number of integral binary n-ic forms in [−H, H]^{n+1} of index ≥ k modulo p is O_ε(H^{n+1}/p^k + p^{n−k+ε}) (27); for D = ∏ p_i^{k_i} and C = ∏ p_i, those of index ≥ k_i modulo every p_i number O_ε(c^{ω(C)}H^{n+1}/D + C^ε ∏ p_i^{n−k_i}) (28), which is O(c^{ω(C)}H^{n+1}/D) if C < H^{1+δ} with 0 < δ < 1/n (29).

items.name: Weil's bound for complete exponential sums
items.statement: For a polynomial Q over F_p of degree m with 1 ≤ m < p, |Σ_{c ∈ F_p} e^{2πiQ(c)/p}| ≤ (m − 1)p^{1/2} (Weil [45]).

items.name: Proposition 30: Fourier transform of w_{p,σ} on monic polynomials
items.statement: For monic polynomials and σ as in Proposition 26: ŵ_{p,σ}(0) = p^{−k}/#Aut(σ) + O(p^{−(k+1)}); ŵ_{p,σ}(g) = O(p^{−(k+1)}) for g ≠ 0 if d < n; and O(p^{−(k+1/2)}) if d = n, by grouping translates x ↦ x + c and Weil's bound. Retain 1 ≤ d ≤ n and p > n; see E24.
items.sourceStatement: For monic polynomials and σ as in Proposition 26: ŵ_{p,σ}(0) = p^{−k}/#Aut(σ) + O(p^{−(k+1)}); ŵ_{p,σ}(g) = O(p^{−(k+1)}) for g ≠ 0 if d < n; and O(p^{−(k+1/2)}) if d = n, by grouping translates x ↦ x + c and Weil's bound.

items.name: Corollaries 31–33: equidistribution of monic polynomials of large index
items.statement: The number of integral monic polynomials of degree n in [−H, H]^n of index ≥ k modulo p is O(H^n/p^k + p^{n−k−1/2+ε}) (31); with several primes, O_ε(c^{ω(C)}H^n/D + C^ε ∏ p_i^{n−k_i−1/2}) (32); and O(c^{ω(C)}H^n/D) when C < H^{1+δ} with 0 < δ < 1/(2n − 1) (33). Here H ≥ 1, p_i are distinct primes > n, D=∏p_i^{k_i}, C=∏p_i. For the final Corollary 33 estimate require k_i ≥ 2, as in the source.
items.sourceStatement: The number of integral monic polynomials of degree n in [−H, H]^n of index ≥ k modulo p is O(H^n/p^k + p^{n−k−1/2+ε}) (31); with several primes, O_ε(c^{ω(C)}H^n/D + C^ε ∏ p_i^{n−k_i−1/2}) (32); and O(c^{ω(C)}H^n/D) when C < H^{1+δ} with 0 < δ < 1/(2n − 1) (33).

items.name: Integral points of a hypersurface in a box
items.statement: If h ∈ Z[x_1, …, x_m] is nonzero, the number of x ∈ [−H, H]^m ∩ Z^m with h(x) = 0 is O(H^{m−1}) (Schwartz–Zippel; [7, Lemma 3.1]).
items.locator: §5 Case III, p. 25; §6 Case III, p. 28 (arXiv v3)

items.name: A nonzero polynomial over a field has at most its degree many roots
items.statement: A nonzero polynomial over F_p has at most its degree many roots. For squarefree C, CRT multiplies such residue-class counts. The application to Disc_x(x^n+…+a_n) gives at most (n−1)^{ω(C)} possible a_n mod C once item 56 supplies its nonzero leading coefficient and gcd(C,n)=1.
items.sourceStatement: A nonzero polynomial of degree d over F_p has at most d roots; with the Chinese remainder theorem, Disc(f) ≡ 0 (mod C) has at most (n − 1)^{ω(C)} solutions a_n modulo a squarefree C coprime to n.
items.note: The library supplies the root count and CRT; the discriminant specialization is routed as missing in item 56.

items.name: Divisor bound
items.statement: A nonzero integer N ≪ H^{O(1)} has O_ε(H^ε) divisors, and c^{ω(N)} = O_ε(N^ε) for fixed c.
items.locator: §5 Case III, p. 25; Theorem 20 proof, p. 15 (arXiv v3)
items.note: AN.5 plans divisor problems among multiplicative functions.

items.name: Counting k-powerful numbers with multiplicative weights
items.statement: For fixed k ≥ 2 and fixed positive integer c, the positive k-powerful integers D ≤ X number O_k(X^{1/k}), and for Y ≥ 2, Σ_{D>Y, D k-powerful} c^{ω(D)}/D = O_{k,c}(Y^{−(k−1)/k}(log Y)^{c−1}). In particular the squarefull tail is O_ε(Y^{−1/2+ε}).
items.sourceStatement: The number of k-powerful D ≤ X is O(X^{1/k}), and Σ_{Y < D, D k-powerful} c^{ω(D)}/D = O(Y^{−(k−1)/k} (log Y)^{c−1}); for squarefull D, Σ_{D > Y} c^{ω(D)}/D = O_ε(Y^{−1/2+ε}).
items.note: Neither the k=1 harmonic tail nor N=0 is included. This is a multiplicative-function estimate owned by AN.5.

items.name: Local density of polynomials with prescribed discriminant
items.statement: For squarefull (resp. k-powerful) D, the monic f of degree n with |Disc K_f| = D satisfy congruence conditions modulo the radical C of D of density O(c^{ω(D)}/D), with c depending on n (c = q(k, n − k) in §6). Apply the tame index congruences at p>n; the finitely many p≤n require a separate uniform bound on their degree-n discriminant exponents and absorption into constants depending on n. Do not identify their full wild valuations with the mod-p geometric index.
items.locator: §5 Case I, p. 23; §6 Case I, p. 26 (arXiv v3)
items.sourceStatement: For squarefull (resp. k-powerful) D, the monic f of degree n with |Disc K_f| = D satisfy congruence conditions modulo the radical C of D of density O(c^{ω(D)}/D), with c depending on n (c = q(k, n − k) in §6).
items.note: The small-prime step is recorded as a supplier obligation in review-gaps, not silently asserted proved.

items.name: Polynomials cutting out a fixed field (Lemke Oliver–Thorne)
items.statement: A number field K of degree n with primitive associated Galois group arises as K_f for at most O(H log^{n−1}H/|Disc K|^{1/(n(n−1))}) monic f with coefficients in [−H, H] ([27, Prop. 2.2]; for general G the saving is u = 0).

items.name: Density of quartic and quintic discriminants (Bhargava)
items.statement: The number of number fields of degree ≤ 5 with absolute discriminant at most X is ∼ cX for an explicit c > 0 ([4], [5]).

items.name: Proposition 34: divisibility for mod p reasons forces a derivative to vanish
items.statement: If p is prime, h∈Z[x_1,…,x_n], and h(c+pd)≡0 mod p² for every d∈Z^n, then every first partial derivative of h at c vanishes modulo p (take d=0 and each coordinate vector and expand mod p²). For h=Disc_x(x^n+a_1x^{n−1}+…+a_n), take a squarefree C supported on p>n with C²|h for mod-C reasons. Then C divides ∂h/∂a_n and the double discriminant Disc_{a_n}(h). The adapter must prove deg_{a_n}h=n−1, leading coefficient ±n^n and nonvanishing of the double discriminant by the specialization x^n+a_{n−1}x+a_n.
items.sourceStatement: If h ∈ Z[x_1, …, x_n] and h(c_1 + pd_1, …, c_n + pd_n) ≡ 0 (mod p²) for all d ∈ Z^n, then ∂h/∂x_n(c) ≡ 0 (mod p). Applied to Disc(f): if C | Disc(f) for mod-C reasons then C | ∂Disc(f)/∂a_n and C | DD(a_1, …, a_{n−1}) := Disc_{a_n}(Disc_x(f(x))), which is not identically zero (f = x^n + a_{n−1}x + a_n).
items.note: The earlier extraction weakened C² to C incorrectly. Remove p≤n before dividing by the leading coefficient. The general Taylor step, universal-discriminant identities and nonvanishing specialization need separate declaration nodes.

items.name: §5 Case I: C ≤ H^{1+δ} and D > H^{2+2δ}
items.statement: The monic f with |a_i| ≤ H, primitive G_f ≠ S_n, C ≤ H^{1+δ} and D > H^{2+2δ} number O(H^{n−1}): each squarefull D contributes O(c^{ω(D)}H^n/D) by Corollary 33, and the sum over squarefull D > H^{2+2δ} is O_ε(H^{n−1−δ+ε}).

items.name: §5 Case II: C ≤ H^{1+δ} and D ≤ H^{2+2δ}
items.statement: These f number O(H^{(2+2δ)(n+2)/4}·H log^{n−1}H/H^{(2+2δ)/(n(n−1))}) = O(H^{n−1}) for n ≥ 6, and O(H^{2+2δ}·H log^{n−1}H/H^{(2+2δ)/(n(n−1))}) = O(H^{n−1}) for n = 4, 5, provided δ is small enough (δ = min{1/(2n), 1/60} serves every n ≥ 4; the paper's δ = 1/(2n) fails for n = 4 and n = 6, see E6). The weighted sum over field discriminants must be justified by dyadic summation or partial summation of F_n(G,X); it is not obtained by replacing each D^{-u} by X^{-u} in a range D≤X.
items.sourceStatement: These f number O(H^{(2+2δ)(n+2)/4}·H log^{n−1}H/H^{(2+2δ)/(n(n−1))}) = O(H^{n−1}) for n ≥ 6, and O(H^{2+2δ}·H log^{n−1}H/H^{(2+2δ)/(n(n−1))}) = O(H^{n−1}) for n = 4, 5, provided δ is small enough (δ = min{1/(2n), 1/60} serves every n ≥ 4; the paper's δ = 1/(2n) fails for n = 4 and n = 6, see E6).

items.name: §5 Case III: C > H^{1+δ}
items.statement: These f number O(H^{n−1}): for p | C, f mod p has a triple root or two double roots, so C | DD(a_1, …, a_{n−1}); with A the product of the primes p | C with p > H^{δ/2}, either A ≤ H and a factor B of C in [H^{1+δ/2}, H^{1+δ}] reduces to Case I with D′ > H^{2+δ}, or A > H, A | DD is determined up to O(1) choices and then a_n up to O(1) choices.

items.name: Theorem 1 (van der Waerden's Conjecture)
items.statement: For fixed n ≥ 3, E_n(H)=O_n(H^{n−1}). The preprint's unqualified degree range requires the quadratic exception E26; E_2(H) has order H log H. The n=1 count is zero.
items.locator: Theorem 1, p. 2; proof §5, pp. 23–26 (with §6 for n = 3) (arXiv v3)
items.sourceStatement: E_n(H) = O(H^{n−1}) for every n.
items.note: The review preserves the intended theorem for n≥3 and does not certify every proof supplier; see the closure gaps.

items.name: The three regimes behind Theorem 2
items.statement: Let G≤S_n be transitive, n≥2, k=ind(G)≥2, c=q(k,n−k), a=a(G)>u, 0<δ<1/(2n−1), H≥2 and 2≤Y≪H^{2n−2}. For the associated number fields the three target bounds are: C<H^{1+δ},D>Y gives O(Y^{−(k−1)/k}H^n log^{c−1}H); D≤Y gives O(Y^{a−u}H log^{n−1}H); C>H^{1+δ} gives O(H^{n+1−k}). Here u=1/(n(n−1)) for primitive G and zero otherwise. The last bound has the unresolved finite-projection/elimination obligation E10.
items.sourceStatement: For a permutation group G ⊂ S_n with k = ind(G), c = q(k, n − k), 0 < δ < 1/(2n − 1) and Y ≪ H^{2n−2}: the f with C < H^{1+δ} and D > Y number O(Y^{−(k−1)/k}H^n log^{c−1}H) (22); those with D ≤ Y number O(Y^{a(G)−u}H log^{n−1}H) (23), u = 1/(n(n − 1)) for primitive G and 0 otherwise; those with C > H^{1+δ} number O(H^{n+1−k}) (24), through index strata cut out by g_1, …, g_k.
items.note: Intransitive groups do not have the field-count input; E17 redirects them to Theorem 7. The k=1 endpoint must be handled separately instead of summing a divergent k-powerful tail.

items.name: Theorem 2: counting polynomials with Galois group G
items.statement: For transitive G≤S_n with n≥2, k=ind(G), admissible a=a(G)>u, c=q(k,n−k), u=1/(n(n−1)) if primitive and zero otherwise, put θ=(1−1/k)/(a+1−1/k−u) and B=max(c,n−1). The corrected target is N_n(G,H)=O_G(min{H^{n+1−k}+H^{n−(n−1)θ}(log H)^B, H^{(2n−2)(a−u)+1}(log H)^{n−1}}), for H≥2. For k≥2 the balancing logarithm is b=(c−1)(1−θ)+(n−1)θ, so B is safe; k=1 needs a separate endpoint argument.
items.sourceStatement: For every permutation group G ⊂ S_n, with k = ind(G), a = a(G), u as above and θ = (1 − 1/k)/(a + 1 − 1/k − u), N_n(G, H) = O(min{H^{n+1−k} + H^{n−(n−1)θ} log^{b}H, H^{(2n−2)(a−u)+1} log^{n−1}H}), where b = (c − 1)(1 − θ) + (n − 1)θ ≤ max{c − 1, n − 1} and c = q(k, n − k). (The paper states log^c H in the middle term; b > c can occur, see E11.)
items.note: E11 proves that the printed comparison b<c fails, not that the smaller-log counting theorem is false. E17 gives an actual counterexample to the intransitive scope. This remains a target contingent on E10's unfilled proof step.

items.name: Corollary 3(a): power savings for primitive groups
items.statement: For primitive G ⊂ S_n, G ≠ A_n, S_n: N_n(G, H) = O(H^{n−2}) for n ≥ 10 (and N_9(G, H) = O(H^{7.06})); O(H^{n−2.5}) for n ≥ 16; O(H^{n−3}) for n ≥ 28; O(H^{n−3.5}) for n ≥ 56 by the paper's argument (printed n ≥ 53, see E13), and for n ≥ 1090 without CFSG.
items.note: The 53–55 cases are unestablished by the displayed argument, not disproved. The corrected range n≥56 is conservative; preserve the source target n≥53 for a separate group-theoretic check. E12 preserves n≥28 by splitting elemental/non-elemental groups.

items.name: Corollary 3(b): non-elemental primitive groups
items.statement: If G is non-elemental primitive then N_n(G, H) = O(H^{b√n log² n}) for an absolute b > 0.
items.note: The non-elemental Galois companion and resolvent-counting interfaces need their own detailed nodes; the target is retained, not certified closed.

items.name: Corollary 3(c): elemental primitive groups
items.statement: If G ≠ A_n, S_n is elemental primitive then N_n(G, H) = O(H^{n − bn/log² n}) for an absolute b > 0 (O(H^{n−b√n}) without CFSG).

items.name: Zarhin's theorem on hyperelliptic Jacobians
items.statement: If f ∈ Z[x] of degree n ≥ 5 has Galois group A_n or S_n, the Jacobian of y² = f(x) has endomorphism ring Z (over Q̄, hence over Q).
items.note: Zarhin, Hyperelliptic Jacobians without complex multiplication, Math. Res. Lett. 7 (2000), pp.123–132, opening statement: degree n≥5 and geometric endomorphisms. The old note about Q-endomorphisms in small degree did not address the geometric claim and was removed; see E25.

items.name: Corollary 4: hyperelliptic Jacobians with extra endomorphisms are rare
items.statement: For fixed n ≥ 5, among smooth curves y²=f(x) with f monic irreducible of degree n and integer coefficients bounded by H, at most O_n(H^{n−bn/log²n}) of the polynomial parameters yield Jacobians with End over Q̄ larger than Z, for a suitable absolute b>0. This counts parameters, and implies the corresponding upper bound on isomorphism classes.
items.sourceStatement: Among y² = f(x) with f monic irreducible of degree n and |a_i| ≤ H, at most O(H^{n − bn/log² n}) Jacobians have endomorphism ring larger than Z.
items.note: Retain the n≥5 hypothesis from Zarhin. The distinct bounds for imprimitive, non-elemental and elemental groups must all enter this deduction.

items.name: Abelian number fields of prime degree (Mäki, Wright)
items.statement: a(C_p) = 1/(p − 1) is admissible: the number of cyclic fields of prime degree p with discriminant at most X is O(X^{1/(p−1)})

items.name: Corollary 5: cyclic polynomials of prime degree
items.statement: For a prime p, N_p(C_p, H) = O(H²).

items.name: Galois number fields (Ellenberg–Venkatesh)
items.statement: For a finite group G with |G|>4 and a fixed number field K, the number of Galois G-extensions of K with norm of the relative discriminant below X is O_{K,G,ε}(X^{3/8+ε}). The author copy of Ellenberg–Venkatesh, Proposition 2.8, provides this statement.
items.sourceStatement: For a finite group G with |G| > 4, the number of Galois G-extensions of a number field K with norm of discriminant < X is O_{K,G,ε}(X^{3/8+ε}) ([18, Prop. 2.8]; Prop. 1.3 of the published version, for each n > 4). For |G| ≤ 4 the exponent is 1 (|G| = 2) or 1/2 (|G| = 3, 4).
items.note: Removed the unsupported blanket |G|≤4 claim: for the regular Klein four group a pure O(X^{1/2}) estimate misses logarithms. No low-degree assertion is imported here.

items.name: Corollary 6: regular permutation groups (corrected)
items.statement: If G is a regular permutation group of degree n = |G| > 4 whose order has no prime factor 2 or 3, then N_n(G, H) = O(H^{3n/11+1.164}). As printed (every regular G) the statement fails for n = 2, and Theorem 2 does not give it when 2 or 3 divides n (see E15).

items.name: Theorem 7: intransitive groups
items.statement: Let G≤S_n be intransitive with orbit sizes n_i and transitive quotient images G_i≤S_{n_i}. Suppose N_{n_i}(G_i,H)=O(H^{α_i}(log H)^{β_i}) for H≥2, α_i>0 and β_i≥0. Put A=max_i α_i and s=Σ_{α_i=A}(1+β_i). Then N_n(G,H)=O(H^A(log H)^{s−1}). Use H₊ including the leading coefficient, and overcount all tuples of irreducible factors; common splitting fields can give any subdirect product, so no exact product-group counting equality is asserted.
items.sourceStatement: Let G be intransitive on n letters, G ⊂ G_1 × ··· × G_k a subdirect product of transitive G_i on n_i letters, and N_{n_i}(G_i, H) = O(H^{α_i} log^{β_i}H). Then N_n(G, H) = O(H^{max α_i} log^{s−1}H) with s = Σ_{α_i = max α}(1 + β_i).
proofSteps: Factor a separable f over Z into its monic irreducible factors. Their Galois groups are the orbit quotient images of G.
Mahler measure and item 11 give ∏H₊(f_i)≤C_n H₊(f), so put factor heights into dyadic bins 2^{j_i}, with Σj_i≤log₂(C_nH).
The number of tuples in these bins is bounded by ∏2^{α_i j_i}(1+j_i)^{β_i}, using cumulative counts, without differentiating them.

For α_i<A sum the exponentially decaying factors 2^{−(A−α_i)j_i}(1+j_i)^{β_i}. For the r indices α_i=A the simplex sum over total degree gives the factor (1+log H)^{Σβ_i+r−1}. Sum the outer geometric tail to get H^A.
items.note: E4, E20 and E21 correct the notation, zero-height exception, and invalid shell-count inference. The hypotheses α_i>0,β_i≥0 cover all applications retained here.

items.name: Corollary 8: G × M_11
items.statement: For G≤S_k with k≤8, or with k=9 and G≠S_9, the corrected target is N_{k+11}(G×M_11,H)=O(H^{8.686}). Also N_11(M_11,H)=O(H^{8.686}), using ind(M_11)=4 and a(M_11)=2.5+ε for sufficiently small positive ε. The unqualified k≤9 assertion is false for G=S_9; see E16.
items.sourceStatement: For G ⊂ S_k with k ≤ 9, N_{k+11}(G × M_11, H) = O(H^{8.686}); in particular N_11(M_11, H) = O(H^{8.686}), using ind(M_11) = 4 and a(M_11) = 2.5 from Theorem 20.
items.note: The fixed-degree-nine S_9 family has order H^9 after multiplication by one fixed M_11 polynomial. Use the positive exponent margin to absorb logarithms and ε. This application inherits the general-counting proof gap.

items.name: Non-monic van der Waerden
items.statement: For fixed n ≥ 3, let E*_n(H) count degree-n integer polynomials a_0x^n+…+a_n with a_0≠0, all coefficients bounded by H and Galois group other than S_n. The target is E*_n(H)=O_n(H^n). The source says the methods extend, without a separate proof; the nonmonic integral-order and leading-coefficient arguments remain a gap.
items.sourceStatement: The number E*_n(H) of f = a_0x^n + ··· + a_n with max|a_i| ≤ H and Galois group ≠ S_n is O(H^n); the paper asserts this follows by the same methods and gives no separate proof.
items.note: Do not derive this from Lemma 24 without its corrected integrality hypothesis, and do not include degree-dropping a_0=0 terms in the degree-n definition.

routes.reason: ST.3 owns counting theorems for number fields by degree, discriminant and Galois group, with low-degree cases organised independently of general conjectures. The paper imports Schmidt's bound with its small trace-zero element, the Lemke Oliver–Thorne bound, Bhargava's quartic and quintic densities, the Mäki–Wright abelian counts and the Ellenberg–Venkatesh Galois-field bound, and states them through Malle's F_n(G, X) and a(G). The paper's own field counts (Theorems 20 and 25) go to the Part II, since they need the index theory built there. Item 34 now explicitly separates a small trace-zero element in an arbitrary field from its primitivity-dependent generator consequence; item 70 is restricted to |G|>4. No low-degree logarithms are silently dropped.

IG.2 proves Hilbert irreducibility over number fields; the density form E_n(H) = o(H^n) for monic polynomials ordered by height is its first counting consequence, as PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-22 also routes its monic height version here.

SF.5 constructs intersection products after Fulton; Bézout's bound for a zero-dimensional complete intersection in projective space is the basic instance, used here only to bound the solutions of the power-sum system (7).

routes.title: Galois groups of polynomials, Part II: counting integer polynomials by Galois group
routes.brief: Extend the Tau Ceti roadmap Galois groups of polynomials (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/PolynomialGaloisGroups), importing its root actions, blocks, primitivity, Frobenius specialization and S_n realizations. The new direction is fixed-degree integer coefficient boxes, distinct from the growing-degree laws of PolynomialGaloisGroupsPartIIRandomPartitions. This brief is NOT ready for a design job: the review rejects the route until the recorded closure, splitting and elimination gaps are discharged. Retain the original source targets and their corrected scopes: E_n(H)=O(H^{n−1}) for n≥3, with the separate quadratic H log H case; item 62's transitive-group bound with B=max(q(k,n−k),n−1), k=ind(G), u=1/(n(n−1)) for primitive G and zero otherwise, and θ=(1−1/k)/(a+1−1/k−u); Corollary 3 with certified numerical thresholds 10,16,28,56 while preserving 53–55 as an unresolved source target; geometric Jacobian endomorphisms only for n≥5; prime cyclic groups; regular groups of order>4 coprime to 6; the subdirect-product bound of item 72; and G×M_11 only for k≤8 or proper G<S_9 at k=9. Layers: permutation index and primitive-group bounds; monic index strata and finite projections; primitive and non-elemental field-count adapters; coefficient-space weights and Fourier cancellation; the three-case sieve; and the application bounds. General k-powerful arithmetic and weighted tails are imported from AnalyticNumberTheory AN.5, and the lattice Poisson theorem from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0. Import field counts and small trace-zero elements from ArithmeticStatistics ST.3, the height form of Hilbert irreducibility from IG.2, Weil's bound from FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums FF.2, tame/wild discriminants and Dedekind–Kummer from upstream LocalFieldsRamification and NumberFieldArithmetic, Bézout from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5, and Mahler measure/Newton identities/Schwartz–Zippel/Jordan special cases from the pinned libraries. Do not re-plan these suppliers. Name and prove the additional finite-projection, integral-spreading, lattice-point and small-prime adapters before accepting §6 Case III. Split compound statements and supply each definition's uses, API and tests, plus declaration dependencies, suggested files and planets. The nonmonic extension needs a separate proof respecting leading coefficients and integrality; it is a recorded gap, not a consequence of the current monic lemma.
routes.reason: The parent Tau Ceti roadmap owns the permutation representation of a polynomial, blocks and primitivity, and Sₙ over ℚ, but no layer counts polynomials by Galois group or develops the index of a permutation group. The random-polynomial Part IIs proposed by PAPER-BARYSOROKER-KOUKOULOPOULOS-KOZMA-23 treat growing degree with fixed coefficient laws, a different regime from the fixed-degree boxes here. The paper's own field counts stay in this Part II rather than ST.3, which would otherwise import its index theory and create a cycle. The broad direction is justified, but its current proof closure and declaration granularity are not: this review rejects activation while preserving the proposed owner and explicit continuation obligations.

AN.5 owns multiplicative functions, divisor estimates and weighted counting of integer sets. The positive k-powerful predicate and c^{ω(D)} tail estimate are general analytic-number-theory inputs, also relevant to arithmetic statistics and sieve consumers. Prove them once here for k≥2 and fixed positive integer c; the polynomial-counting Part II imports them together with item 51. The reviewed AUDIT-06 and fresh pinned searches do not supply these sharp weighted estimates.

AL.0 owns Schwartz/Fourier theory and Poisson summation with explicit character and measure conventions. Item 43 is the finite-dimensional real lattice instance with a finite periodic twist, needed by the polynomial coefficient boxes; it extends the pinned one-dimensional Poisson theorem by iteration and absolute convergence. Its corrected grouping includes every zero-residue frequency (E23). The reviewed AUDIT-14 AL.0 row records only one-dimensional lattice Poisson in the baseline. Keep polynomial-specific weight functions and finite-field cancellation in the Part II.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 16, inequality (6), pp. 10–11 (arXiv v3)
sourceIssues.printed: The source treats even m and k with y = m/2 separately, writing f(m, k, y) = …. In every other case it claims σ fixes some element of {1, …, m}, labelled m, and uses f(m, k, y) = f(m − 1, k − 1, y) + f(m − 1, k, y) to invoke induction.
sourceIssues.correction: Treat the fixed-point-free case with k odd separately (then no k-subset is σ-invariant, so f = C(m, k) ≥ (4/5)C(m, k)), and run the induction over 1 ≤ k ≤ m/2 with (m, k) = (4, 2) excluded: at m = 2k, f(2k, k, y) = 2f(2k − 1, k − 1, y) by complementation when σ has a fixed point, and C(2k, k) − C(k, k/2) ≥ (4/5)C(2k, k) for even k ≥ 4 when it has none.
sourceIssues.reason: 'Otherwise' also covers m even, y = m/2, k odd, where σ has no fixed point. And for m = 2k + 1 the step invokes (6) at (m − 1, k) = (2k, k), outside the stated range 1 ≤ k < m/2; (6) fails at (4, 2, 2) (f = 4 < 4.8), though the step only reaches (2k, k) for k ≥ 3, where the complementation argument proves it. (6) itself was checked by enumeration for all m ≤ 14, and Theorem 16 is unaffected.
